questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *

questions.answer: All the above were considerations for going on exchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy as the host university (ETH Zürich) were good at providing information and introduction meetings. I will say however, the Canton of Zürich provide a lot of their information in German which is not the most helpful. I used google translate and that worked fine. Also asking people around me worked well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had information meeting on what to do and sent out emails also. Upon registration in the Kanton of Zürich, they also provided a lot of information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There was a form I could fill on the ETH website from a student housing association called WOKO and then I got assigned housing maybe 2 months before arrival (housing through WOKO is not guaranteed)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived very close to the Hönggerberg campus whic his were I was primarily. But, I also had classes at the city center and at Irchel campus. So keep this in mind when signing up for courses. The housing I lived in was with other exchange students, were we shared one single industrial kitchen between 170 students. That took some time to get used to. Be prepared to share with others, but it also means you make a lot of friends very fast. If possible, try to live with other people as it is nice to have friends to ask questions and do on hikes / other activities with

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses online and can change courses in the first weeks. The process is pretty easy. Block courses have different registration process that they inform you about over email.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had an introduction meeting explaining it

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted. I was enrolled at the department of biology were they have block courses (6 ects courses that are mostly lab based). These are space limited and you rank them according to preference. Exchange students are prioritised last, but I ended up with courses relevant to my studies (all of them either my first or second choice).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress. But also just get it done early, and you can always change it within the first weeks.
There was a german course 2 weeks before semester start. This was very worth it as I made a lot of friends from the start.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My course load was very heavy (the block courses take up a lot of time). The level is however not the highest. Especially the course Membrane biology  was not very interesting for me (it was mostly structural biology). The biology and biochemistry students have had a lot of "engineering" courses, so their cell biology is not at the level we are used too (although they might be better at coding and statistics). 
The lecture based courses i attended were only lectures with no classroom hours. This makes the courses not that engaging. I had immunology I at ETH and Cancer and the Immune system at UZH (you have to apply a bit earlier to be approved to take courses at UZH, but it is possible). Both of these courses were 3 ects with two hours a week. The courses were intersting and a bit difficult, the exam was multiple choice and not very difficult.  They also don't really have a syllabus (at least for the courses I attended). Mostly you can follow the lecture recording and powerpoints slides for immunology I. Cancer and the Immune system was more interesting but required a previous understanding of immunology (so be aware of that). Also, reading review papers about cancer (like the three reviews about the hallmarks of cancer by Hanahan is a good starting point).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Cancer and the immune system was a master level course. Requires knowledge of immunology but otherwise alright. 
The block courses require a lot of time physically in the lab. But they are not that hard theoretically. The students are not used to reading papers so things like journal club are not at a very high level. If you can follow the courses for molecular biomedicine back home then it should be fine if you are taking courses at the department of biology (unless it is something that requires coding and math).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH has better teaching with classroom hours. The block courses however are pretty cool. You get to try a lot of techniques and do experiments that are out of budget for UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
551-0351-00L Membrane Biology
551-1525-00L Cancer Progression: Mechanisms, Targets and Therapeutic Approaches
BIO 251 Cancer and the Immune System
551-1515-00L Insulin Signaling
551-1511-00L Parallels Between Tissue Repair and Cancer
551-0317-00L Immunology I

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All the courses except membrane biology. Keep in mind that Immunology I also has a part II in the spring. But it should be more than enough to compensate for the lack of immunology in the course "Human fysiologi"
The following block courses were nice to gain experience in tissue culture and a broad array of assays and techniques:
551-1525-00L Cancer Progression: Mechanisms, Targets and Therapeutic Approaches
551-1515-00L Insulin Signaling
551-1511-00L Parallels Between Tissue Repair and Cancer

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation in Zurich is arounf 60 francs a month if you are under 25. For transportation in switzerland you can get a friends pass with up to 3 other people under 25. This costs around 640 DKK in total => 160 DKK pr. person. This gets you a full day of free transportation in Switzerland. This is ideal for going on hikes. 
They also have a half fare card for traveling that can be worth it for some gondola lifts up mountains if you like hiking.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a sports association that is free. I know a lot of my friends enjoyed that.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had some parties, sports association and parts of the central campus has some art installlations (they had a picasso exhibition once).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, traveling in Switzerland and in the neighbouring countries. Block courses are nice, but also remember to spend your time traveling while the weather is nice. You can do quite a lot in a weekend. In January I only had one exam to prepare for, so I bought a GA travel card for one month that let me travel anywhere in Switzerland for free. I went for a lot of hikes, skiied and went to Paris also. Highly recommended.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking and see the cities. There are endless hikes and mountains to see.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Switzerland is not that different from Denmark. So it was pretty quick

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not socialise a lot with local students as i lived with other exchange students and did most things with them. It was really nice as they also don't have many obligations and were always up to go on hikes and other trips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Kanton of Zürich sends letters in German which is a bit annoying

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and the cleanliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go for the nice university but also enjoy the nature!
Things can be a bit expensive in Switzerland, so it is not a bad idea to have some money saved (but, if you cook everyday then it is not crazy). 
Depending on your studies the courses might be at a very different level. For biology it was not as bad as i feared. But, for some other studies like chemistry and physics I did hear that it was challenging.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your time there, and since courses are transferred as passed/failed you can chill a bit and have some fun outside of studying.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made along the way. We had a lot of potlucks, parties and hikes / trips to other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My course load was pretty heavy. In winter the sun sets pretty early so there were some days were i did not see the sun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you are a EU national you can be exempted from paying insurance!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
